# Tarnmere Homes: Scheme of Delegation (extract)

Version 3, adopted by the Board January 2025. Sections 4 and 6 only.

4.2 The Operations & Investment Committee (OIC) may approve contracts with a total value over the contract term of more than £250,000 and up to £1,000,000. Above that figure the Committee recommends to the Board.
The Committee approved the award to Vantry Systems Ltd as recommended, subject to the Company Secretary being satisfied with the exit and data return clauses.

### Costs (Option B)
| Item | £ |
|---|---|
| Licence, hosting and support, five years | 690,000 |
| Implementation services (call-off) | 235,000 |
| Contingency (held by Finance, not committed) | 90,000 |
| **Programme total including contingency** | **1,015,000** |

reading: Scheme of Delegation 4.2: the OIC 'may approve contracts with a total value over the contract term of more than £250,000 and up to £1,000,000'. The act: the Committee approved the award to Vantry Systems Ltd; Paper 4 costs the five-year licence, hosting and support at 690,000. The body that acted (the Operations & Investment Committee) is the body the instrument names. The act does not cite the scheme. Not shown: the contract's 'total value' as 6.1 defines it; Paper 4 also shows a 235,000 implementation call-off and a programme total including contingency of 1,015,000, 4.1 reserves a contract or commitment over 1,000,000 to the Board, and no advice under 6.2 on aggregation is in the material. This finding is not a judgement on whether the act was within the Committee's powers.

# Tarnmere Homes: Scheme of Delegation (extract)

Version 3, adopted by the Board January 2025. Sections 4 and 6 only.

4.5 Where an approval would otherwise be given by the Board or a committee and the next meeting is too late to avoid material harm or loss, the Chair and the Chief Executive acting jointly may take the decision. The decision must be recorded in the decision log and reported to the next meeting of the body that would ordinarily have made it.

Margaret, see below. I think we should move it to 1 October. Waiting for the September Board would mean we either go live unprepared or stay on the wrong date in the meantime and tenants get the wrong number. Alison, is this the urgent action route?

Sorry for the delay, I was away. Fine. Agreed, go with 1 October, and keep the agency cover going until then. Please make sure Kestrel and the union are told and that it's logged and goes to September.

reading: Scheme of Delegation 4.5: where an approval would otherwise be given by the Board and the next meeting is too late to avoid material harm or loss, 'the Chair and the Chief Executive acting jointly may take the decision', to be recorded in the decision log and reported to the next meeting. The act: Duncan Faraday (Chief Executive, per the Board minute of 21 May) and Margaret Oyelaran (Chair, per the same minute) agreed 1 October by email; the stated harm of waiting is going live unprepared or tenants getting the wrong number. The persons who acted hold the posts the instrument names. Invocation is also evidenced, as a paragraph number ('4.5') given in the thread, and is carried as an authority contribution in HC-003. Later material records the log entry (DL-26-014) and the Board noting it on 17 Sep (DL-26-015). Not shown: that a change to a date the Board had itself resolved is 'an approval [that] would otherwise be given by the Board' — the Company Secretary's view was 'I think 4.5 covers a change of date, though it is the Board's resolution'.

Orchard extension

Any such extension is to be reported to the next meeting of the OIC.' The act: six months from 1 Oct at about £48k plus about £3k, verbally agreed, noted under the name P. Check with Karen'); and the report to the next OIC meeting, which the decision log shows as open at 30 September 2026.

fragments.content: Orchard remains live. Calder extended the licence by six months to the end of March 2027, so a February go-live is covered.

Orchard (supplied by Calder Software) has been in use since 2014. Calder will stop supporting the current version when the licence ends on 30 September 2026. Repairs, rents, tenancy and complaints records all sit in Orchard, and there are 31 interfaces to other systems.
